findings.title: A field presented as a quotation of sarif-projection-contract.v15 is not that quotation, and its own accepted predecessor carries the string byte-exact.
findings.subjectValue: d9-exit-contract.v1.14 already records this golden. This artifact binds the projection to that golden. It does not mint a new D9 code or a new exit number.
findings.liveSourceValue: D9 v1.14 already records this golden. This artifact binds the projection to that golden. It does not mint a new D9 code or a new exit number.
findings.delta: The opening token 'D9 v1.14' is replaced by 'd9-exit-contract.v1.14'. The remainder is identical.
whyThisIsNotCosmetic: The subject declares the standard it breaks. basedOn.d9v114.role states 'Quoted, not rewritten.' A field named quotedV15OwnerOfValues that is in fact rewritten contradicts the artifact's own stated method in the one place a reader checks that method.

The accepted predecessor in this exact lineage sets the byte-exact precedent. sarif-fc-outfail-golden-bind.v1.json carries the identically-named field quotedV15OwnerOfValues == v15's ownerOfValues, tested by ==. That predecessor is Claude ACCEPT 0/0 and is pinned by this subject at 5bc60d33…, verified. The successor silently altered a quoted string its own predecessor had frozen, with no note anywhere in the artifact.

It is the sole exception in the artifact. Nine other quoted or *Verbatim fields were tested by == against their live sources and all nine are byte-exact. The drift is an anomaly against the subject's own uniform discipline, not a house convention.

It has downstream mechanical consequence. D-294 (ADOPTED at HEAD) established that a citer's asserted values are compared against the cited bytes, and that any changed projected value requires a successor. A same-named field whose value differs between bind.v1 and golden.v1 is exactly the drift that machinery exists to catch, and a later reader diffing this field against v15 cannot tell from the artifact whether v15 moved or the citer restated it.
findings.whyNotMustFix: The substitution is semantically faithful and expands an abbreviation into the artifact's own pinned filename rather than inventing an identifier; d9-exit-contract.v1.14 is a real file pinned in recordedInputs at a digest this review verified. No D9 code, exit number, recipe, or authority claim is affected, and no attack-list bullet is reached. The defect is custody of quoted prose, not truth of the claim.
findings.minimumRepair: Restore v15's exact string as the value of quotedV15OwnerOfValues. If the expanded artifact name is wanted for clarity, keep the quotation byte-exact and carry the expansion outside it — for example a sibling note stating that v15's 'D9 v1.14' denotes docs/coop/artifacts/d9-exit-contract.v1.14.json at 8dd33038…, which is already pinned in recordedInputs. Either repair is a single string and moves no other byte.
